description: Running the clippers up the length of a sheep sat back against both knees, the wool folding away ahead of them in one unbroken sheet.
Peeling the last of a whole wool coat clear with a free hand and letting it drop whole onto the swept plank floor.
Working round the shoulder with hand shears, the wool coat opening like a seam parting along a stitch line.
Tipping a broad cream-woolled sheep gently back onto its haunches and settling both knees into position before picking up the clippers.
Coaxing the clippers round the curve of a blocky black-faced sheep's belly with one slow careful arc, the pale cream skin beneath emerging clean and even.
Finishing the last long pass up the spine of a speckle-nosed sheep and straightening the arm to let the whole wool coat fall open in one blanket.
Forking an armload of wool up onto a heap already higher than one shoulder, the loose fibres catching and spreading as they land.
Treading a bundle of wool down into a plain open-topped wooden crate and getting twine round it before it springs back up.
Throwing a whole wool coat out flat over the heap and watching it billow and then settle, smoothing one edge down with a forearm.
Picking a muddy tuft from the edge of a wool coat spread across the swept plank floor, holding it between two fingers at arm's length.
Sweeping a broad drift of loose wool together with a besom broom, the pile growing into something respectable with each stroke.
Walking a sheep backwards out of the holding pen by the chin, the animal stepping along quite willingly one deliberate hoof at a time.
Lifting a hurdle out of the way with one knee and a shoulder, holding it sideways to fit through a gap just barely wide enough.
Shaking a bucket once so the whole pen of grown sheep swings round toward the sound in a loose uneven mob, two at the back still deciding.
Steadying a freshly clipped-bare sheep with one flat hand on its stubbled side while it works out that it is considerably narrower than it was a moment ago.
Guiding a broad cream-woolled sheep through the shed doorway with a hand at the shoulder, both of them ducking slightly out of long habit.
Straightening up with both hands pressed hard into the small of the back and eyeing the twelve grown sheep still waiting against the far rail.
Drinking from an enamel mug and discovering wool in it, pulling the strand out slowly and regarding it with no great surprise.
Picking loose wool off both forearms by the handful and dropping it onto the heap, finding more under the wrists than seemed possible.
Leaning right over the top rail on both elbows to count the holding pen twice because the first answer and the second answer disagree.
Swinging the yard gate wide and stepping well back out of the rush, one hand still resting on the top bar as the clipped-bare goat-slim mob pours past.
Crouching on the packed earth to watch the clipped-bare stubbled mob go past, counting under the breath while two blocky black-faced ones veer wide of the gate.
Walking the wall line slowly, one hand trailing along the plain weathered timber, counting a loose uneven mob of grown sheep spread across the yard.
Pointing once at the holding pen and then folding both arms and leaving the entire business entirely to the collie.
Standing aside with arms folded while the collie brings the next four grown sheep up the race at a calm, measured trot.
